title: Which products are less than one?
description: Four products, seven times zero point six, zero point seven times zero point six, zero point seven times six and zero point zero seven times zero point zero six, are checked for the ones less than one, and then found by counting the digits after the point, the same way as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number below one times a number below one gives a product below one, while a number below one times a number above one can give more than one. Watch for students who think any product with a decimal is below one.

source: Without doing any multiplication, find which of these products is less than 1: (a) 7 × 0.6 (b) 0.7 × 0.6 (c) 0.7 × 6 (d) 0.07 × 0.06. The products are 4.2, 0.42, 4.2 and 0.0042.
video_script.why: The child has seen that a number below one takes a part of the other number and now uses it to pick products less than one.
video_script.substitution: the book's four products, seven times zero point six, zero point seven times zero point six, zero point seven times six, and zero point zero seven times zero point zero six
video_script.anchor: Four products from the book, to be sorted into the ones less than one
video_script.payoff_line: The products less than one are now known.

final_answer.spoken: The second and the fourth products are less than one. The four products are four point two, zero point four two, four point two and zero point zero zero four two

maths_rules: (a) 7 × 0.6: digits after the point 0 + 1 = 1; 7 × 6 = 42; so 4.2, more than 1 since half of 7 is 3.5
(b) 0.7 × 0.6: 1 + 1 = 2; 7 × 6 = 42; so 0.42, less than 1 since both numbers are below 1
(c) 0.7 × 6: 1 + 0 = 1; 7 × 6 = 42; so 4.2, more than 1 since half of 6 is 3
(d) 0.07 × 0.06: 2 + 2 = 4; 7 × 6 = 42, a zero is put in front of 42 to make four digits; so 0.0042, less than 1
a number below 1 times a number below 1 is below 1
video_script.design: One idea: both numbers below one give a product below one. Assumes the digit rule and the part idea. The four products stay all video; the decimals appear only on the answer beat.
